newsitem.title: GERMANY: Yeltsin flies back to Russia after German visit.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin flies back to Russia after German visit.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin left for home on Friday after a three-day visit to Germany during which he expressed optimism Moscow could settle its row with NATO over the alliance's eastward expansion.
A spokesman for Stuttgart airport said Yeltsin's plane departed just after 0900 GMT for the Black Sea resort of Sochi.
Yeltsin's spokesman said on Thursday the president and his wife may spend a few days there before returning to Moscow next week.
Yeltsin appeared cheerful when he left his hotel for the airport. He waved to hotel staff who had gathered to see him off and walked steadily, getting into his car unaided.
The Russian president, 66, had looked pale and tired after talks on Thursday with Chancellor Helmut Kohl, his personal friend and political ally, in the spa resort of Baden-Baden.
He came away declaring optimism that their special relationship could unblock the snags and allow a signing date of May 27 date for a NATO-Russia treaty in Paris to go ahead.
Wile Yeltsin, who has had major heart surgery and pneumonia in the last five months, takes a break, intensive negotiations will be needed to make that a "reality", a Kremlin spokesman said.

At a ceremony to accept a "Man of the Year" award from the German media on Thursday night, Yeltsin renewed his demand for a binding treaty giving Moscow guarantees that the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation's expansion into eastern Europe would not threaten Russia's security.

He repeated his criticism that making former Soviet bloc states members of the western pact risked reopening divides in Europe after the efforts Russia had made to introduce democratic reforms and end the ideological conflict of the Cold War.

"Broadening military alliances, advancing NATO's military infrastructure towards Russia's borders, will not create a united peaceful Europe," Yeltsin said, reading his speech clearly but showing more signs of fatigue than in other recent appearances since he returned to work from illness two months ago.
